transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

A single click as a fridge cycles on or off can be normal. Repeated clicking every few minutes while the freezer is warming is not: it usually means the compressor is trying to start, then its overload protection is cutting it out. The most common area is the compressor start relay/overload; less commonly the compressor itself is sticking or overheating. A supply or control fault is also possible. 1. When it is clicking, listen at the lower back without removing any covers. If it is a brief hum followed by a click from the black compressor cylinder, that points to a start/overload or compressor-start problem. If there is no hum at all, control or power supply becomes more likely. 2. Check the plug is fully home and test the wall socket with a lamp or another appliance. If the socket is unreliable or trips the electrics, stop using the fridge and have the supply checked. If the socket is sound, the fault is likely within the fridge-freezer. With the fridge switched off and unplugged, also make sure any accessible rear/underneath grille is not clogged with dust and that it has a few centimetres of clearance from the wall. Poor ventilation can make a marginal compressor cut out on heat, but it would not normally explain persistent repeated clicking on its own. Keep freezer food in a separate freezer or cool boxes if it is starting to soften. If the clicking returns after the basic checks, this needs an appliance engineer: they can test the start device and compressor safely, rather than guessing at parts.

Thank you. When it clicks there is a very brief hum first, then silence for a few minutes, and the click comes from the small box on the side of the compressor at the bottom back. I tried another wall socket and it did exactly the same, and the fridge is plugged straight into the wall with no extension lead. The back is a bit dusty but it has a gap from the wall. There is no burning smell and nothing has tripped. Does that point to a particular part?

Yes — that pattern points most strongly to the compressor start relay/overload device: the small box on the side of the compressor. The brief hum means the compressor is being asked to start; the click a few moments later is usually the overload cutting it out when it cannot get going. Because it behaves the same from a second wall socket, an external supply fault is much less likely. Dust may make overheating worse, so carefully vacuum accessible dust from the rear/underneath with it unplugged, but dust alone would not usually cause this repeated hum-then-click cycle. The important alternative is a compressor that is becoming hard to start internally. The distinction is made by testing the start device and compressor windings with the appliance isolated; if the start device tests sound or is substituted and it still only hums then clicks, the compressor is the likely fault. Do not buy a part on the symptom alone. An appliance engineer should test the start relay/overload first — it is the most likely and usually simpler repair. If the compressor itself is at fault, that is a sealed-system repair and is often worth comparing against replacement on a fridge-freezer of this age. Keep any softening freezer food in another freezer or cool boxes in the meantime.
